newsitem.title: UK: Med gasoline steady to up, traders eyeing US arb.
newsitem.headline: Med gasoline steady to up, traders eyeing US arb.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were largely steady on Thursday, traders said.

Gasoline prices were steady to slightly higher with anticipated buying for Nigeria supporting well supplied low octane product while tight supplies, Italian buying and a more attractive arbitrage to the U.S. underpinning prices for higher octane oil.

Traders said they were eyeing an opening arbitrage to the U.S. with NYMEX crude holding around half of Wednesday's one cent a gallon gains and cheaper freight costs making transatlantic shipment look more attractive.
They said worldscale rates for 30kt transatlantic cargoes had fallen in the past week from around worldscale 200-220 to 170.
Demand for higher octane material into Italy pegged Eurograde cargoes steady around $190/$192 a tonne cif Med.
Naphtha markets were further dulled by an Industry function but traders reported sufficient end-user buying interest to balance fresh Russian cargo avails.
Weaker crude and refiner selling though left prices slightly softer at around $169/$173 a tonne cif Med.
Gas oil was flat in a fairly quiet market.
EN590 cargoes were steady as tight supply continued to support premiums. Premiums were talked around quotes fob hi +$2.0/+$3.0 cif NWE.
"I don't think premiums will get much above $3 because there isn't that much demand either," said one trader.
The last know EN590 cargo deals done were priced at around quotes fob hi +$3.25 and +$3.60, traders said.
Russian material was well supplied with diffs talked around quotes fob hi -$1.50/-$1.0 cif NWE.
Italian islands material was talked 75 cents to $1.0 above there.
High sulphur fuel oil was a steady with traders saying not to much availability was around.
There was unconfirmed talk of an independent trader selling its cargo late on Wednesday out of Bilbao to a Spanish refiner but no further details were immediately available.
Low sulphur was said to be flat, with traders saying not too many avails were around apart from a cargo out of Cartagena and a second one out of Libya.

An independent trader seeking a cargo of low sulphur fuel in the North for the past few days said it bid a high number in the Mediterranean, $110 cif, adding that the seller was still far away, at $113.
But other traders said they doubted these higher numbers, saying it may be an attempt to drive up the market to price its own material into the Med.
